dedupe_keys.name: nlr hive highly integrated vehicle ecosystem agent based simulation of mobility service fleets and their ev charging networks

description: HIVE is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) framework that simulates the operations of mobility service provider fleets such as ride-hailing. Contents: it models vehicles and charging or fuelling stations as individual agents, so scenarios can vary operating areas, vehicle types and fleet mix, EV charging and fuelling station networks, dispatching algorithms, economic and policy factors and customer willingness to pool or delay travel. Outputs include fleet performance, energy use, vehicle usage and level of service at vehicle, vehicle-type or fleet level, and electrical load profiles and utilisation for single stations, groups of stations or the whole network. Producer: NLR Transportation and Mobility Research; described in an NLR technical report (2021). Coverage: any city with travel demand data; published work covers Austin, Texas, and New York City ride-hailing fleets (iScience, 2022). Format and access: open source framework on GitHub, linked from the NLR page. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): BSD-3-Clause. Caveats: results depend on the travel demand and dispatch assumptions supplied. Simulation uses: sizing public fast-charging for electrified fleets, charging load profiles for grid studies, and agent-based evaluation of fleet operations. Related records: platform-nlr-evi-x-ev-charging-infrastructure-modelling-suite and model-matsim.
